target_customer: Pharmaceutical and biotech partners and public antimicrobial resistance funders who would license or co-develop new antibiotic candidates
problem: Bacteria evolve resistance to antibiotics faster than new drugs are developed, so each new antibiotic loses effectiveness. Evolvere aims to design antibiotics using co-evolutionary protein interaction data and AI so that resistance is anticipated.
business_model: Therapeutics R&D; likely licensing or partnership of drug candidates (not stated by sources)

founders.name: Adam Winnifrith
founders.background_notes: YC page describes his work as bioengineering, protein AI and automation. Search snippets from Oxford BioEscalator say he studied Biochemistry at Corpus Christi.

founders.name: Piotr Jedryszek
education: University of Oxford, biology (YC page says biology and computational biology background)

founders.name: Weronika Slesak
founders.background_notes: Describes her work as using evolution as an engineering tool.

competitors.name: Phare Bio
competitors.what: Nonprofit using generative AI to design new antibiotics
competitors.traction_then: Publicly profiled in 2024 as designing new antibiotic compounds

technical_complexity.rationale: Predicting bacterial resistance evolution and designing drugs against it is research-grade, and requires wet lab validation and years of preclinical work for a 3 person team.

defensibility.rationale: Co-evolutionary datasets and models could be a moat and drug candidates can be patented, but nothing public shows validated candidates as of the batch.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Antibiotics are a weak commercial market that big pharma largely left, so little copying risk; no acquisition found as of the research date.

market_need_then: Antimicrobial resistance was widely described as a growing global health crisis, with government grant programs (Innovate UK, AMR programmes) funding early work. Commercial market for new antibiotics is weak, which is a known problem.

branding.domain_note: Uses evolverebiosciences.com, a descriptive suffix domain, not exact .com for the name alone

identity.logo: A logo exists on Oxford BioEscalator pages; no source describes it
identity.voice_and_tone: Emoji heavy YC description with plain language about bacteria and resistance

branding.community_and_virality: Oxford community coverage (BioEscalator, college news) of the Oxford biohackathon win; no wider virality found

brand_strength.rationale: Name echoes evolve, but searches found no press about the brand itself and only university and aggregator coverage.

outcome_analysis: Evolvere is an Oxford spinout that won a university biohackathon, joined the BioEscalator, took an Innovate UK grant and entered YC in Summer 2024. No priced equity round, exit or shutdown was found, so the outcome is still open. The scientific team has strong domain fit, but antibiotics are a hard commercial market and the company has not shown validated drug candidates in public sources.
notes: Company website returned HTTP 503 and the BioEscalator article returned 403, so only search snippets were available for those. UKRI record shows a 50,000 GBP grant offer (currency GBP, so amount_usd left null; grant year 2022 is an estimate from the BioEscalator timeline and is not stated in the snippet). Aggregators (VCBacked, healthcarediscovery.ai) list about 500K USD total raised with a September 2024 pre-seed attributed to YC, and Dealroom lists a 125K seed with no date; these are unverified and not recorded as rounds. A healthcarediscovery profile says it found no Innovate UK award, which conflicts with the UKRI record. Education for Jedryszek and Slesak taken from search snippets quoting BioEscalator and the YC page, not opened directly.
